title: Charred sweetcorn scrambled eggs on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Corn, butter, spring onions, eggs, milk, bread and chives are all plain whole foods a grandparent would have had.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket, and corn cobs are cheap in August.

basic_kitchen.reason: A frying pan, a bowl, a whisk and a toaster or grill are all ordinary kit, and scrambling eggs suits a beginner.

works.reason: Eight eggs, two cobs and four slices of toast make a sensible breakfast for four, and charring the corn before scrambling the eggs gently on low heat will work as written.

honest_times.reason: Stripping two cobs, slicing spring onions and beating eggs fits within 15 minutes, and the 5-minute char plus a quick scramble fits a quick breakfast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Corn cobs and wholemeal bread match their ids, and the steps use every listed ingredient and seasoning with nothing unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh sweetcorn at its August peak is the point of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant flourishes.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, sweetcorn and wholemeal toast make a filling, real-food breakfast a family would happily repeat.
